evaluation_dimensions.name: Architecture
evaluation_dimensions.description: Technical stack, service decomposition (micro‑services vs monolith), redundancy patterns, and multi‑region failover design. Highlights differences in compute (GPU/TPU), storage layers, and orchestration tools. [DOC-001]

evaluation_dimensions.name: Enterprise Latency / Throughput
evaluation_dimensions.description: Measured end‑to‑end processing latency and sustained throughput under peak Q2/Q3 workloads, including batch vs real‑time pipelines. Captures both advertised benchmarks and observed performance during outage windows. [DOC-002]

evaluation_dimensions.name: Pricing Predictability
evaluation_dimensions.description: Structure of usage‑based fees, tiered discounts, and any hidden surcharge (e.g., egress, premium support). Evaluates variance between quoted rates and actual invoices during the outage period. [DOC-003]

evaluation_dimensions.name: Advertised vs. Actual SLA
evaluation_dimensions.description: Comparison of vendor‑published service‑level agreements (availability, MTTR, compensation) against empirically observed uptime and remediation times in Q2/Q3. Includes analysis of SLA breach notifications. [DOC-004]

evaluation_dimensions.name: On-Prem / Hybrid Readiness
evaluation_dimensions.description: Degree to which the platform supports on‑premises or hybrid deployments, including edge compute options, data residency controls, and integration complexity. Relevant for customers who migrated during the outage window. [DOC-005]

evaluation_dimensions.name: Customer Sentiment & Trust
evaluation_dimensions.description: Qualitative and quantitative sentiment derived from support tickets, public forums, NPS scores, and third‑party review sites. Tracks trust erosion or recovery post‑outage. [DOC-006]

sources.purpose: Capture timestamps, duration, and vendor statements for each outage event.
Obtain first‑hand reports of impact, root‑cause details, and remediation actions.
Validate outage timelines and cross‑reference with vendor disclosures.
Extract disclosed outage costs, compensation clauses, and forward‑looking reliability commitments.
Harvest sentiment signals and anecdotal evidence of trust erosion.
Baseline advertised architecture, SLA terms, and pricing models for comparison.

actions: Set minimum impact threshold (≥5% of affected customers or ≥30 min downtime).
Restrict to Q2 and Q3 2024 calendar windows.
Scrape status page archives and API logs.
Export ticket excerpts via secure VPN access.
Pull monitoring alerts from third‑party services.
Standardize severity levels (Critical, High, Medium, Low).
Apply a taxonomy (Hardware Failure, Software Bug, Network Issue, Capacity Exhaustion, Human Error, External Attack).
Tag each incident with primary and secondary causes.
Map each incident to the six evaluation dimensions.
Calculate observed latency/throughput deltas versus advertised benchmarks.
Derive SLA breach rates and compensation payouts.
Run NLP sentiment scoring on ticket comments and public reviews.
Track NPS trend before, during, and after outages.
Highlight root‑cause patterns unique to each competitor.
Formulate actionable recommendations for the client’s positioning.

competitor_profiles.name: CloudScale AI
competitor_profiles.positioning: Enterprise‑grade agent orchestration plane offering a Gateway for semantic caching, token optimization, and intelligent load balancing across 14 LLM backends. Targets mid‑to‑large engineering enterprises migrating multi‑agent systems to production.

competitor_profiles.name: DataPulse Systems
competitor_profiles.positioning: Real‑time streaming data infrastructure and feature store that connects Apache Kafka, Flink, and vector databases directly to autonomous agent execution engines. Serves financial institutions, fraud‑detection teams, and high‑frequency real‑time analytics workloads.

competitor_profiles.name: NexusOps Technologies
competitor_profiles.positioning: Autonomous AIOps platform that automates IT incident triage, telemetry correlation, and self‑healing runbook remediation using multi‑agent graphs. Focused on DevOps, SRE, and platform‑engineering organizations managing Kubernetes at scale.

competitor_profiles.name: Veloce Security
competitor_profiles.positioning: GenAI runtime firewall that intercepts prompt injection, jailbreak attempts, and PII leakage in sub‑15 ms, protecting agentic applications for healthcare, legal, and other compliance‑sensitive enterprises.

quotes.quote: CloudScale reduced our Groq and OpenAI token costs by 28% within the first month. However, documentation for custom Python middleware is sparse, and we experienced two 3-hour outages in Q2 where support disputed our 10x SLA credit claim citing upstream cloud network degradations.

The semantic cache hit rate hovers around 22% in production, which is lower than the advertised 40%. The UI dashboard is intuitive, but on-prem installation took four weeks instead of the promised 48 hours.

DataPulse is unrivaled for real-time latency. Our fleet routing agents query fresh sensor states in 6ms. Be careful with high-volume Kafka topics, however; overage fees doubled our invoice in month three before we configured filtering.
Reduced our MTTR from 45 minutes to 11 minutes for recurring database and pod connection incidents. The safety guardrails are solid—it has never accidentally executed an unsafe command in production.

Veloce caught three sophisticated indirect prompt injection attempts during our clinical pilot. The false positive rate on medical abbreviations is slightly annoying (around 4%), but their customer support helped tune custom bypass dictionaries quickly.

outages_and_incidents.description: Two separate three‑hour service outages occurred in Q2; the customer’s request for a 10× SLA credit was denied by support, who attributed the failures to upstream cloud network degradations.
On‑premises deployment took four weeks, far exceeding the promised 48‑hour installation window, indicating a significant delivery delay.

praise_and_positive_outcomes.description: Achieved a 28 % reduction in Groq and OpenAI token costs within the first month of usage.
Delivered sub‑10 ms query latency for real‑time sensor data, highlighting strong performance for high‑frequency routing workloads.
Reduced mean time to recovery (MTTR) from 45 minutes to 11 minutes and provided reliable safety guardrails that prevented unsafe command execution in production.
Successfully detected three sophisticated indirect prompt‑injection attempts during a clinical pilot, demonstrating effective security controls.
User interface dashboard described as intuitive, facilitating easier monitoring and management.

usability_and_friction_points.description: Sparse documentation for building custom Python middleware creates integration friction for developers.
Observed semantic cache hit rate of 22 %—significantly below the advertised 40 %—and prolonged on‑prem installation time.
High‑volume Kafka topics triggered overage fees that doubled the invoice in month three before proper filtering was applied.
False‑positive rate of approximately 4 % on medical abbreviations caused minor annoyance, requiring manual tuning of bypass dictionaries.
